title: Claims Intake Guidance — Filing a Claim under the New Home Builder Warranties
content:
This guidance states the filing rules that apply when a homeowner claims a defect under Bridgewell's New Home Builder Warranties.

## Filing rules

1. Claims are filed in writing by the current owner.
2. A claim is accepted only when it is filed no later than the program's claim notice period, in calendar days, after the defect is discovered, counting from the day after the discovery date the homeowner states with the boundary day included.
3. The defect must have been discovered within the coverage phase for its claim category; a defect discovered during a phase may still be filed up to the program's grace period, in calendar days, after that phase ends.
4. Cosmetic surface defects (paint, finishes, scratches, chips) are covered only when reported within the program's cosmetic reporting period, in calendar days, after the closing date.
5. When the homeowner had emergency work done to stop further damage, the claim says so, and the cost is reimbursed under the warranty's payment and settlement terms.

Each claim covers one defect and records the claim number, the filing date, the discovery date the homeowner states, the claim category (workmanship, water penetration, systems, structural or appliance), the homeowner's description of the defect in the homeowner's own words, and whether emergency work was done before filing.

## Rule 2: the notice period

- **Clock starts:** the discovery date, as the homeowner states it; this date is taken from the homeowner's statement, and the claim is tied to the homeowner's own warranty.
- **Counting:** day one is the day after the discovery date; the last day of the period counts.
- **Comparison:** the filing date must be no later than the last day of the period.

| Discovery date stated (hypothetical) | Day one | Last day of a 30-day period | Filed on | Accepted under rule 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 August | 5 August | 3 September | 3 September | Yes |
| 4 August | 5 August | 3 September | 4 September | No |

## Rule 3: discovery within the phase, and the grace after it

| Discovered | Filed | Meets rule 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Within the phase for the claim category | While that phase is running | Yes |
| Within the phase for the claim category | After the phase ends, within the grace period | Yes |
| Within the phase for the claim category | After the phase ends, beyond the grace period | No |
| After the phase for the claim category has ended | At any time | No |

**Hypothetical case.** A workmanship phase ends on 14 May. A homeowner discovers a workmanship defect on 10 May and files on 5 June. Under a 30-day grace period the defect discovered during the phase may be filed through 13 June, so rule 3 is met; under a 30-day notice period counted from 11 May the last day for filing is 9 June, so rule 2 is met as well.

## Rule 4: cosmetic surface defects

**Hypothetical case.** Under a program whose cosmetic reporting period is 60 calendar days, a chip in a countertop finish reported within 60 calendar days after the closing date can be covered; the same chip reported later is not covered as a cosmetic surface defect.
